messages:
sofia: quick sync — following the hedging RFC, i want to nail down semantics when a tenant is in 'runoff' (backfill) vs normal burst credits. two questions: (1) should hedged requests for runoff tenants use reserved burst credits? (2) how do we surface cancellation to downstream serving so we don't double-bill tokens?

ajay: +1 need this. my gut: hedges should never consume a tenant's reserved credits if the original was queued under runoff policy. otherwise we're eating their backfill quota.

liam: is there a hard requirement that hedged requests observe the same admission path? if hedges are routed to a fast replica that ignores runoff it could bypass controls. maybe hedges should carry a small admission token header so we can check accounting at the front door.

kate: we already add X-Tenant-Admission: <lease-id> in provisional flows. extend that to hedges and cancellation. then admission service can decide: charge hedge -> deduct; or treat hedge as "no-charge probe".

sofia: exactly. proposal: hedges for runoff tenants get a policy flag: hedge_charge: [charge, probe, reject]. default = probe for runoff. ops can flip to charge for critical SLAs.

liam: sounds reasonable. needs safety for race conditions though. if the original request eventually runs and succeeds, and the probe also consumed tokens, auditing will see double usage unless we tie responses together. we need a canonical request id and a short-lived KV to mark billed outcome.

sofia: agreed. sketch: attach hedged requests to parent_id and set cancellation_grace_ms (default 200ms). flow: if parent completes, write parent_id->winner to cheap-store; hedges check store before final charge. cheap-store TTL = 5s.

ajay: pseudo-config for ops console:
```
runoff_policy:
  hedge_charge: probe
  cancellation_grace_ms: 200
  hedges_per_request: 1
```

kate: practicality note: cheap-store ops need to be fast and partition-tolerant else we open windows where both sides bill. maybe use an in-memory LRU with replication to local shards and eventual consistency — audit can reconcile later and credit back if double-bill detected.

sofia: tradeoff callout: weaker consistency -> cheaper latencies but higher audit churn. strong consensus -> fewer billing discrepancies but more p99. we should start with weak+audit for initial rollout and a strict mode behind a feature flag for strategic customers.

ops-bot: FYI deploy-bot scheduled a canary of hedging-v3 to the us-west pool at 10:30am.

deploy-bot: canary started (job id: canary-hedge-v3-4305). monitoring: hedged-success-rate, duplicate-billing-count, admission-latency.

liam: one last thought: probes vs charge also affects fairness scheduling. probe hedges should be admitted at lower priority to avoid stealing capacity from paying traffic. we should add priority_tag: probe|normal|critical so scheduler makes informed choices.

sofia: yep. next steps: ajay + liam to draft updated admission headers + cheap-store contract. kate to mock ops console flags. i'll open follow-up RFC with config + rollout plan. thanks all :thumbsup:
